issues.description: The problem statement and the template declare that PersonService.addParent(Person person, Person parent) should return the persisted Person (the result of personRepository.save(...)), and multiple callers (PersonResource and the service tests) expect a returned Person. However, in the solution implementation PersonService.addParent is declared to return void while callers still assign its result. This return-type mismatch makes the solution inconsistent with the specification and template and would cause compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's PersonService.addParent method return Person (change signature to 'public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)') and return the saved entity (e.g. 'return personRepository.save(person);'). This will align the solution with the template, the problem statement, and the existing callers/tests.

issues.description: The conceptual operation addParent(Person, Person) is specified in the problem statement and template to return the persisted Person (the result of personRepository.save(...)), but the solution's PersonService implementation declares addParent with a void return type. PersonResource (and some tests) call or expect addParent to return a Person. This mismatch of the addParent API across artifacts creates confusion about the expected behavior and return value of the same conceptual operation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addParent method signature consistent across artifacts. Prefer restoring the return type to Person and return the saved entity (e.g., return personRepository.save(person);). Update any implementation, usages in PersonResource, and tests to expect and propagate the returned Person. Alternatively, if the intended design is to return void, update the problem statement, template method signature, PersonResource calls, and tests to consistently use void and not expect a returned Person.
